package_info.package_versions: New variant (2020, as described in report)
package_info.why_malicious: Cerberus is a sophisticated Android banking Trojan distributed via a compromised Mobile Device Management (MDM) server. It leverages enhanced Remote Access Trojan (RAT) capabilities to exfiltrate sensitive data, including banking credentials and SMS (such as 2FA codes), by abusing device permissions and accessibility services. This results in a severe compromise of device integrity, user privacy, and organizational security.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (immediately after installation via MDM, during app initialization)
execution_context.file_location: Android app code (APK, main activity or initialization routine)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, immediately after installation via MDM, the code requests permissions for reading and receiving SMS, internet access, reading contacts, writing to external storage, and enabling accessibility services, allowing the app to access sensitive user data and device controls for subsequent exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Requesting a broad set of sensitive permissions, especially SMS, internet, and accessibility service, is highly indicative of malicious intent, as it enables interception and exfiltration of confidential data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps, including banking apps, should only request permissions essential for their advertised functionality. Requesting both SMS and accessibility service permissions together, especially at install time, is atypical and signals potential abuse.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate financial apps may request SMS permissions for OTP auto-fill, but rarely in combination with accessibility service and broad storage access, and not immediately after silent MDM installation.
key_indicators: Simultaneous request for SMS, internet, and accessibility service permissions
Permission request occurs immediately after silent installation
Request for WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and READ_CONTACTS without clear user-facing justification

execution_context.file_location: Android app code (background service or SMS receiver component)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SmsManager smsManager = SmsManager.getDefault(); String sms = getSmsContent(); sendToC2(sms);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, in a background service after permissions are granted, the code reads incoming SMS messages (including 2FA codes) and transmits their content to a remote command-and-control (C2) server over the internet, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting SMS messages in the background and sending their content to an external server is a classic behavior of banking Trojans targeting 2FA and credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps may read SMS for OTP auto-fill, but should never transmit SMS content externally, especially without user interaction or notification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may access SMS for local OTP parsing, but do not exfiltrate SMS data to remote servers.
key_indicators: Automated exfiltration of SMS content to external C2 infrastructure
No user notification or consent for SMS data transmission

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on device boot or app start, after accessibility service enabled)
execution_context.file_location: Android app code (main activity or accessibility service handler)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, on device boot or app start after accessibility service is enabled, the code checks for accessibility service activation and, if enabled, escalates privileges to perform actions on behalf of the user and evade detection or removal.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing accessibility services to escalate privileges and automate user actions is a well-documented technique in Android malware for persistence and evasion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate use of accessibility services is limited to assistive technologies and should not be used for privilege escalation or to bypass user controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility services are used by apps for aiding users with disabilities, but not for automating privileged actions or maintaining persistence against removal.
key_indicators: Programmatic check for accessibility service status
Invocation of privilege escalation routines upon accessibility service activation
Persistence mechanisms tied to accessibility service abuse

attack_chain.action: A compromised MDM server silently pushes the Cerberus APK to employee Android devices without user interaction.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious Cerberus app is installed on target devices, bypassing normal user consent.

attack_chain.action: Upon first launch, the Cerberus app immediately requests a broad set of sensitive permissions, including SMS, internet, contacts, storage, and accessibility service.
attack_chain.leads_to: The app gains access to sensitive data sources and device controls necessary for further malicious activity.

attack_chain.action: Cerberus operates a background service that reads incoming SMS messages (including 2FA codes) and exfiltrates their content to a remote C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers receive intercepted credentials and authentication codes, enabling account compromise.

attack_chain.action: Cerberus abuses the accessibility service to escalate privileges, automate user actions, and maintain persistence on the device.
attack_chain.leads_to: The app can perform privileged actions, evade removal, and maintain long-term control over the device.

behavioral_signatures: Android app installed via MDM requesting SMS, internet, and accessibility service permissions in combination
Background service reading and exfiltrating SMS messages to external servers
Abuse of accessibility service for privilege escalation and persistence
file_indicators: APK distributed via MDM with manifest requesting android.permission.BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, READ_SMS, and INTERNET
Presence of package names or signatures associated with Cerberus variants
network_indicators: Outbound connections from device to known Cerberus C2 domains or IP addresses
Unusual HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing SMS or credential data to external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android apps installed via MDM that request SMS, internet, and accessibility permissions together. Detect background services accessing and transmitting SMS content. Flag apps abusing accessibility services for privilege escalation or persistence. Correlate outbound network traffic to known Cerberus C2 infrastructure and analyze for exfiltration of SMS or credential data.
